name: structure-coaching
title: Structure signals coach GREEN, and VALIDATE reports them beside the slice score
outcome: GREEN gets structure coaching when it adds a file, VALIDATE reports structure findings beside the slice score, and the main agent runs each slice through the RED, GREEN, and VALIDATE agents.
done_when: A spike on zenagent/agencheck records the precision of each uncertain signal, and the engineer checks 10 labels for each signal
A spike transcript shows one real coach message that carries a structure signal from the second runner in habit_coach.py
shared/structure_signals.py reports a crowded folder with its groups, a name family, a generic name, and each kept coach signal, and reads its limits from .cobuilder/structure-signals.json
shared/structure_boundary.py reports each import or path string in a new file that names a context outside the allowed dependencies of its boundary.yaml
A coach signal fires only for a file that is untracked or added since the merge-base. Tests cover an uncommitted file and a branch with no merge-base
The output of shared/structure_signals.py names each path that the script did not analyse
The coach gives structure signals for each extension, stays silent about smells for an unscanned extension, and repeats no finding in a session. It has no cap on structure findings
The engineer approves the coaching language, the message for each signal and the Structure block format, before the coach and VALIDATE use it
A test of the effect check covers no attempt file, a pass at attempt 1, and workflow mode, and the check fails for a main-agent slice
shared/structure_evidence.py writes an evidence packet for the slice diff with Python contract drift, boundary edges, vocabulary leads, and each signal that the spike keeps
The attempt file holds a Structure block outside the overall score. It labels each finding, judges contract drift, cohesion, and new dependencies, and a failed attempt passes it to GREEN
The vocabulary agent judges each vocabulary lead against DDD-VOCABULARY.md, and tags a name AVOID only when it means the avoided concept
A replay of three runs or more for each condition, five slices each, records the growth of the largest folder and the follow-on resolve rate
One real slice runs locally from RED to a VALIDATE score, and the transcript is kept
abort_if: The spike shows that a second runner in habit_coach.py cannot put a folder signal into the coach message
A hand label on three repositories gives each of the three signals a precision below 50%. A single signal below 50% is dropped instead
The replay shows no rise in the follow-on success rate, and no gain in folder growth, duplication, silent contract changes, or dependencies across a boundary
The structure work needs a hard block on a write, which ADR-0025 does not allow for the coach

min_work.derived_from: 2 districts (implement, shared), 3 colliding ADRs (ADR-0025, ADR-0012, ADR-0038), 1 boundary rule (implement allowed_dependencies), 3 signals, 6 epics
min_work.note: Decided in chat on 2026-11-10. The engineer kept the GREEN filter, accepted the two coach guards, kept the agent-use effect open for the spike, and rejected slice-loop.js as the default run mode. Draft review round 1 scored 0.63 and round 2 scored 0.75. The session applied the material findings of both rounds. Round 3 in chat on 2026-11-11: the engineer removed the cap, chose the second runner as the only route, added a coaching-language slice for engineer approval, approved the design, and chose one PR. Gate 1 on 2026-11-11: the engineer widened the problem past folders. VALIDATE also judges cohesion and dependencies across a boundary, and a backlog epic E7 builds an import parser and a dependency diagram.

epics.title: The tracer, then shared/structure_signals.py and shared/structure_boundary.py with the coach signals and their tests.
epics.outcome: The stdlib scripts report a crowded folder with its groups, a name family, a generic name, a boundary edge, and each coach signal that the spike keeps, only for new files.

epics.title: A coaching-language slice for engineer approval, then the second runner in habit_coach.py carries the signals to GREEN, with no repeat in a session and no smell output for an unscanned extension. The install writes the default config.
epics.outcome: The engineer approves the coaching language, and a stub-binary test shows a structure signal for each extension, no smell output for an unscanned extension, and no repeat on a second write.

epics.title: The slice loop text makes the main agent spawn the three agents, and verify_gate.py checks one effect that shows the agents ran each slice.
epics.outcome: A blind pass spawns all three agents in manual mode and in workflow mode, and the check fails for a slice that the main agent wrote.

epics.title: shared/structure_evidence.py writes an evidence packet for the slice diff, and VALIDATE judges each finding in an advisory Structure block. The vocabulary agent judges the vocabulary leads.
epics.outcome: The packet holds Python contract drift, boundary edges, and each signal that the spike keeps. The attempt file holds a Structure block with a label for each finding and the three judgments, outside the overall score.

epics.title: A replay of slice plans with the signals on and off, a hand label of the findings, and the decision on scored criteria.
epics.outcome: The evaluation record holds the folder growth, the follow-on resolve rate, and the precision of each signal.

epics.title: Review mode and maintenance mode run each signal on the whole repository, show the folder table and the trend, and write one findings file.
epics.outcome: A review report and a maintenance report each carry the whole-repository findings, ranked by recent change count, and the findings file has a fixed schema.

epics.title: The import graph of E4 becomes a dependency diagram, and the boundary check covers more languages. This epic is in the backlog, after E5.
epics.outcome: The bundle shows a dependency diagram for each context, with each edge that breaks a boundary record marked.

epics.title: An /architect:refactor skill reads the E6 findings file and plans refactor slices. This epic is in the backlog, after E6.
epics.outcome: The skill turns the ranked whole-repository findings into a refactor plan that /implement:start can build.
